This paper examines the expressive power of Constraint Handling Rules (CHR) by analyzing variations in the constraints permitted within rule heads and bodies. We demonstrate that the number of atoms allowed in the rule heads significantly influences expressive capabilities. Additionally, the study explores the relationship between CHR's expressive power and that of the first-order $\lambda$-calculus.

This study investigates the large-scale alignment of galaxy spin axes within the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) DR12, specifically focusing on the dipole axes of these spins. We examine the consistency of these findings across the DR12 sample and previous surveys, including DR7, DR11, and DR12, as well as the 2MASS survey. Our analysis reveals that the galaxy spin direction dipoles identified in DR11 and DR12 are highly consistent with one another and with results from 2MASS. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the dipole axes are statistically significant and robust against variations in redshift ranges and galaxy magnitude limits. Additionally, we observe that the dipole axes derived from DR11 and DR12 are nearly parallel, with a small angular separation of 1.5 degrees.

Few-shot learning (FSL) has emerged as a critical area of research, driven by the need to train models with limited data. While existing FSL methods typically rely on metric learning, they often fail to effectively exploit the intrinsic structure of the data. To address this, we introduce Eigen-Reptile, a new approach that integrates eigen-decomposition into the Eigen map of a prototype-based FSL framework. This method utilizes the eigen-decomposition of a feature covariance matrix to sample feature representations, thereby enhancing the robustness of the FSL process. Specifically, Eigen-Reptile samples features by leveraging the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix, ensuring that the sampled data points align with the primary directions of variance. Furthermore, the method incorporates a novel regularization term to stabilize the eigenvalues and eigenvectors, effectively mitigating issues related to label noise and variations in sample sizes. Experimental results on the standard few-shot learning benchmarks demonstrate that Eigen-Reptile outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

The Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) serves as a prevalent instrument for assessing cognitive function, yet its impact on predicting Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression and survival remains uncertain. This study investigates whether MMSE scores can enhance prediction of AD outcomes and mortality. Using data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), we developed a deep learning model to forecast cognitive trajectories. By integrating MMSE scores with MRI data, we compared the model's performance against a baseline using only MMSE scores. Our findings indicate that combining MMSE scores with MRI data significantly improves the prediction of future MMSE scores, while a similar approach yields comparable results for estimating future Mini-Cog scores. Furthermore, this integrated method outperforms the use of MMSE scores alone in predicting both future Mini-Cog scores and survival rates.

This study examines the prevailing approaches to AI ethics within the existing scholarly discourse. We introduce a novel framework for the ethical evaluation of artificial intelligence and outline a corresponding methodology for the practical implementation of these analyses.

The concept of a trio, which constitutes a Boolean-closed family of languages, was introduced by McNaughton and Zaporożets in 1970. In 1974, McNaughton and Zaporożets demonstrated that the trio of finitary languages, denoted as F, is the unique decidable Boolean-closed family of finite languages. This paper extends the investigation to trio, which are defined as Boolean-closed families of languages over an infinite alphabet, and investigates decidability for this broader context. We establish that the trio of finitary languages is the sole decidable Boolean-closed family of languages over an infinite alphabet. Furthermore, we prove that for any infinite alphabet, every trio is undecidable.

This paper introduces a hybrid channel estimation framework tailored for millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications, combining a neural network (NN) with a traditional least squares (LS) method. The proposed scheme leverages a deep neural network to forecast the channel's sparse representation, followed by an application of a least squares algorithm to derive the precise channel state. By integrating the rapid computational speed of NN-based methods with the accuracy of LS techniques, the hybrid approach achieves superior performance compared to existing schemes. Simulation results demonstrate that this scheme significantly outperforms both pure NN-based and conventional LS-based methods in terms of accuracy. Furthermore, it offers a reduced computational complexity compared to the traditional least squares technique.

Recent discrepancies between the measured and predicted values of $V_{ud}$ and $V_{us}$, which hint at physics beyond the Standard Model, have spurred a surge of interest in $C\!P$-violating neutron decay. This study examines the neutron's $C\!P$-violating electric dipole moment (EDM) within the framework of two-Higgs-doublet models (2HDM). We investigate how the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-non-conserving quark mixing matrix, arising from the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of the $C\!P$-violating phase of

This paper introduces a new network architecture for 3D brain tumor segmentation that leverages dilated convolutional layers to capture expansive receptive fields without increasing parameter count. This approach eliminates the need for downsampling and subsequent upsampling, thereby mitigating information loss during feature extraction. The model's efficacy is validated on the BRATS 2017 dataset, where it achieves a Dice score of 0.89, and is further evaluated on the public TCGA-GBM dataset, yielding a Dice score of 0.89.

This paper introduces a methodology for creating data views that uphold privacy constraints. The objective is to ensure that the resulting views effectively separate private data from shared information, thereby eliminating the risk of accidental data leaks. The approach begins by defining a data view as a query, followed by a discussion on the theoretical foundations of view synthesis. It then outlines the core algorithm and details its implementation. Finally, the work demonstrates the method's application using a real-world dataset.

We present a study of the mid-infrared (MIR) spectral energy distribution (SED) for 100 galaxies within the COSMOS field, utilizing data from the Spitzer Space Telescope. By applying a new method that accounts for dust emission across various wavelengths, we derived the MIR spectral indices for these galaxies. Our findings reveal that the MIR spectral indices of galaxies in the COSMOS field are generally consistent with those of local galaxies. Furthermore, we examined the correlations between MIR spectral indices and radio luminosity, as well as morphological structure. Our results indicate that galaxies exhibiting hot dust emission are predominantly radio-luminous and typically possess disturbed morphologies. In contrast, galaxies lacking hot dust emission display a wide range of morphological structures and radio luminosities. Additionally, we analyzed the MIR spectral indices in relation to the specific star formation rate (sSFR). Our analysis shows that sSFR is positively correlated with MIR spectral indices for galaxies with sSFR > 0.1 Gyr⁻¹, but no such correlation exists for galaxies with sSFR ≤ 0.1 Gyr⁻¹.

Although recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success in various tasks, their capacity to comprehend human moral reasoning remains limited. To address this, we introduce MORALCOT, a novel prompting strategy designed to enhance LLMs' understanding of human moral logic. This method leverages the capabilities of these models to perform zero-shot chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning by constructing a structured, step-by-step chain of moral arguments. To support this process, we developed the MORAL-100k dataset, which consists of 100,000 human moral stories annotated with explicit justifications for moral judgments. This dataset facilitates the generation of structured arguments that capture the nuances of human moral deliberation. Experimental results demonstrate that MORALCOT not only surpasses existing CoT prompting techniques in predicting human moral judgments but also yields more accurate and better-explained moral reasoning.

A valuation ring $ V $ with a residue field $ \overline{V} $ of characteristic $ p $ can be described as the direct limit of valuation rings $ A $ that are $ p $-rings, where the residue rings are perfect fields, utilizing the $ p $-power Frobenius map in the finite extension of $ \overline{V} $. This construction applies to the finitely generated rings $ A $, which are $ \text{Spec}(V) $-schemes. This result is applicable to the construction of the $ \overline{V} $-reduced schemes.

The 2D Dirac equation is fundamental to both condensed matter physics and high-energy physics, finding use in areas such as graphene, topological insulators, and Dirac semiconductors. This study introduces a novel numerical approach for solving the 2D time-dependent Dirac equation. The methodology decomposes the equation into two coupled systems of coupled first-order hyperbolic equations, which are then solved using a finite-difference scheme. The proposed scheme demonstrates second-order accuracy in both space and time. Furthermore, the paper establishes the convergence of the method and demonstrates its stability through rigorous error estimation. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings and confirm the method's efficacy across various applications.

Model Predictive Control (MPC) is a potent method for solving complex optimization problems, particularly in cooperative driving scenarios involving multiple agents. However, its reliance on iterative optimization makes it computationally expensive, often resulting in slow execution times. To address this, we introduce a new approach that substitutes the computationally intensive nonlinear optimization with a lightweight linear model. This linear model is continuously refined using a reinforcement learning strategy based on the optimization errors. Empirical results indicate that this proposed method not only matches the performance of standard MPC but also significantly accelerates execution speed.

The proliferation of social media has enabled the rapid dissemination of information, but this speed often comes with the risk of spreading false or unverified content. This study investigates how social platforms influence users' credibility assessments of news. By examining the impact of social cues, we conducted a user study involving 100 participants who evaluated the trustworthiness of news articles both with and without contextual social signals. The findings indicate that social cues significantly enhance users' ability to distinguish credible news from misinformation. Additionally, we developed a social credibility score to quantify the effect of these cues on trust judgments.

The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and the widespread adoption of 5G technology have enabled the creation of a smart city ecosystem. Within this framework, traffic management systems are evolving to become more intelligent and efficient. This paper introduces a smart traffic management system designed to detect road emergencies, predict congestion, and manage network resources effectively. The system's core innovation is the $\pi$-ROAd (p-ROAD) framework, a mechanism for dynamic resource allocation that responds to road incidents. $\pi$-ROAd utilizes a machine learning model to forecast traffic conditions and adaptively distributes network resources to traffic management nodes based on these predictions. The architecture further incorporates a lightweight, edge-deployed congestion prediction model that delivers rapid results with minimal computational overhead. Additionally, the system features an intelligent traffic light controller capable of adapting to real-time traffic flow. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that $\pi$-ROAd achieves a 90% prediction accuracy for road congestion and reduces the average waiting time for vehicles at traffic lights by 20%.

This study examines the challenges of navigating a robot through a cluttered environment while avoiding collisions with moving obstacles. It specifically investigates the integration of the Artificial Potential Fields (APF) collision avoidance strategy within the Differential Breadth First Search (DBFS) algorithm. The research demonstrates that employing the APF algorithm results in significantly shorter trajectories compared to using the DBFS algorithm alone. Furthermore, the study establishes the effectiveness of the APF algorithm in enabling the robot to reach its destination more rapidly during collaborative operations.

Levels of autonomy and machine intelligence are rising, fundamentally reshaping the built environment. This shift transforms the roles of humans within the urban landscape, creating new challenges for urban planning. To address these issues, the paper introduces a framework for modeling and analyzing the future impacts of autonomous transportation systems. This framework integrates a multi-agent simulation with machine learning to forecast the effects of varying levels of autonomy on urban form. The study demonstrates that increased autonomy can lead to more compact urban structures, thereby reducing the need for urban sprawl.

This study investigates online caching with side information, where a cache of capacity $k$ receives requests over time and receives a prediction for the most probable next item. We analyze how prediction quality, measured by prediction error $E$, influences the competitive ratio. We demonstrate that the standard competitive ratio of $\max\{2, \frac{N}{k}\}$ can be improved to $O(1 + \frac{E + k}{k})$. Additionally, we prove a lower bound of $\Omega(1 + \frac{E}{k})$ for any algorithm, indicating that when prediction is inaccurate, our upper bound matches the lower bound within a constant factor. Our approach introduces a novel framework for online algorithms that integrates a base algorithm with a predictor, formalized as a "hybrid algorithm." This model is versatile, applicable beyond caching to areas like clustering and classification. Specifically, we propose a hybrid algorithm for caching that achieves our upper bound, proving that our bound is tight.

We introduce the Trilateral Attention Network (TrANet), a model designed to enhance semantic segmentation by integrating three complementary information pathways. The first pathway, a standard encoder-decoder, delivers coarse-to-fine hierarchical features. The second pathway employs a pyramid structure to capture multi-scale context. The third pathway utilizes a pyramid attention mechanism to focus on long-range dependencies. By fusing outputs from these three routes, TrANet effectively captures both local and global information, leading to superior segmentation accuracy. TrANet achieves state-of-the-art results on the Cityscapes and PASCAL VOC datasets, offering a more efficient alternative to prior methods.

This paper examines the torsion constraints within the linearized supergeometry of $\mathcal{N}=1$ superspace. By imposing these constraints on gauge fields defined on superspace, we derive a set of corresponding conditions for their restrictions to the supermanifold's $\mathcal{N}=1$ superisotopic slice.

The efficacy of learning models relies heavily on the quality of their training data, which is often difficult to assess due to the opaque nature of the learning process. This paper introduces a new methodology for quantifying the impact of individual training examples on model performance. By analyzing the influence of specific data points, this approach enables the identification of critical samples that significantly shape a model's behavior. We demonstrate that this method is highly effective for evaluating training data, offering insights into the model's decision-making mechanisms. Furthermore, the technique is adaptable to various model types, including deep neural networks, and can be utilized across different domains such as computer vision and natural language processing.

We examine how non-Abelian matrix Berry phases influence quantum charge pumping within the three-dimensional topological surface of a quantum anomalous Hall state. This surface hosts a topological order characterized by a non-Abelian anyon lattice, which, upon 2+1 dimensional reduction, manifests as a topological phase with a non-trivial matrix structure. We demonstrate that the non-Abelian matrix Berry phase is responsible for the quantized pumping effect. Furthermore, we establish that the non-Abelian matrix Berry phase provides a robust mechanism for charge pumping, as it remains invariant against fluctuations in the strength of the topological mass term.

We introduce METRO-LM, a series of Transformer language models ranging from 100M to 1B parameters, trained on a curated dataset of 100TB of web data. These models are trained using a novel, efficient training strategy that employs a hybrid of supervised fine-tuning and self-supervised learning. This approach significantly reduces computational costs and memory requirements compared to standard pretraining, enabling the training of 100M–1B parameter models on a single GPU. Our models achieve competitive results on various benchmarks, including GLUE, WMT, and FLORES, often outperforming larger models with fewer parameters. Furthermore, our 300M and 600M variants exceed the performance of the GPT-2 12B model on multiple metrics. We also demonstrate that METRO-LM can be effectively used for few-shot learning and neural machine translation. Our models are accessible via HuggingFace and HuggingFace Hub.

We introduce a method for determining the topology of a quantum network using only local measurements. This approach is essential for understanding how quantum information travels across the network. By performing a set of local measurements, the network's topology can be recovered with a probability of success that approaches one as the number of measurements increases. This technique is applicable to any network where nodes are connected by quantum channels that facilitate teleportation.

This research investigates how different introduction strategies influence a model's ability to explain visual encodings. We evaluated three methods: (1) presenting examples of the input data, (2) defining features, and (3) defining concepts. We developed a framework to automatically generate these three approaches and tested them using three distinct visualization types: heatmaps, treemaps, and scatterplots. Our findings indicate that showing concrete examples was the most effective strategy for helping audiences understand the explanations provided by these encodings.

Controlling many-body quantum systems through optical means is a rapidly advancing field with significant potential for applications in quantum information and simulation. However, the inherent heating induced by Floquet protocols poses a serious threat to system order. In this study, we introduce a novel approach to mitigate Floquet heating by regulating the energy absorption rates of the constituent particles. We demonstrate that this method is highly effective, particularly in the high-frequency regime, where it enables the realization of a thermal equilibrium. Furthermore, we show that this strategy can be readily implemented using the standard optical lattice model.

Counterfactual reasoning generates plans by altering specific actions to achieve desired outcomes. While prior research has largely focused on designing counterfactuals for single events, practical scenarios often demand coordinated changes across multiple factors. This paper introduces a novel framework for formulating multi-plan counterfactuals that remain robust against uncertainty in model parameters. We define a new metric for plan quality and demonstrate that plans which optimize for this metric maintain their effectiveness despite variations in the parameters. Additionally, we present a method for identifying the minimum set of action variables that, when modified, guarantees the plan's success. We also provide theoretical proofs establishing the optimality of our approach regarding both plan quality and the compactness of counterfactual sets. Empirical evaluations using a real-world dataset confirm that our method produces high-quality, interpretable, and reliable plans.

We investigate the $N=4$ supergravity theory in four dimensions featuring two negative cosmological constants and two electric black hole solutions. This work demonstrates that within this supergravity framework, the $AdS_2\times S^2$ and $AdS_2\times H^2$ geometries emerge as co-extensive forms of a single $AdS_4$ black hole. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between the electric charges of these two $AdS_2$ embeddings and the horizon areas of the resulting solutions.

This paper introduces Cain, a compiler for SCAMP-5 that generates significantly more compact code compared to the SCAMP-5 output. While the code algorithms from Cain are straightforward, the resulting programs are more condensed than those produced by SCAMP-5. Additionally, the document outlines the compilation process and provides empirical evidence through runtime comparisons demonstrating Cain's superior efficiency.
We examine the generalized Witten effect within the framework of quantum gravity, demonstrating that it imposes significant constraints on the spectra of charged states.

We introduce three enhancements to the regret pruning methodology, which is designed to learn Nash equilibria in extensive-form games. The first enhancement involves two new variants of regret pruning that leverage a revised definition of path-averaged regret, surpassing the approach originally proposed by the authors. The second enhancement involves a modification to the regret pruning algorithm that integrates elements of counterfactual regret pruning, specifically utilizing the concept of virtual information sets. The final enhancement consists of a revised regret pruning algorithm that incorporates the "chunking" technique. The paper presents both theoretical and computational findings demonstrating the advantages of these proposed improvements.

This study introduces a novel modal logic designed to expand Aristotle's modal syllogistic through a rigorous treatment of modalities applied to states-of-affairs. This framework enhances our comprehension of the original syllogistic system and establishes the foundation for contemporary applications of modal logic in syllogistic reasoning.

Classical causal inequalities serve as necessary conditions for specific causal structures, such as those where a single cause precedes multiple effects. Violating these inequalities necessitates a minimum detection efficiency, thereby offering a method to certify effectance. In contrast, quantum causal inequalities do not impose such efficiency thresholds. This study demonstrates that quantum causal inequalities can detect causally impossible structures even when detector performance is imperfect. Specifically, we prove that violations of these inequalities under suboptimal conditions can be achieved by employing entangled states across multiple pairs of quantum systems.

This study introduces a dual-critic reinforcement learning framework designed to manage video encoding by simultaneously optimizing rate control and distortion. By employing two independent value functions, the system effectively handles the interplay between rate constraints and distortion. Through the application of soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithms, the framework learns to generate encoding parameters that maximize the long-term expected reward. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach surpasses traditional heuristic methods in both efficiency and performance.

This study investigates the impact of photo-ablation on carbon-rich grains on the gas-phase chemistry within protoplanetary disks. We developed a new chemical model that incorporates photo-ablation rates for both C and O-rich grains, derived from a two-dimensional radiative transfer model of the disk. This approach accounts for the destruction of grains and the subsequent release of their constituent elements into the gas phase. The model was validated against observational data from the TW Hya disk, specifically the C$^+$ and SiO emissions. Our results indicate that photo-abalation of carbon-rich grains sustains a long-lived equilibrium cycle between gas and solid phases. This mechanism is a primary driver of C$^+$ emission in the disk, with the process being most pronounced in the outer regions. Additionally, we found that photo-abalation of O-rich grains significantly influences the gas-phase chemistry of the inner disk, where temperatures are high enough to prevent grain destruction.

We introduce NeuralCut, a new approach for selecting cuts in mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) using deep learning. Unlike traditional baselines that rely on heuristics, NeuralCraft selects cuts based on the latent features of a neural network. This model is trained on a dataset of past branching decisions and their corresponding outcomes, learning to predict cuts that effectively reduce the search space. Our experiments on the MIPLIB 2020 benchmark demonstrate that integrating our method with CPLEX 12.10 yields solutions up to 100 times faster than current best-in-class techniques.

The superconducting behavior of the topological superconductor candidate Td-Mo1-xIrxTe2 was investigated using specific heat and electrical transport measurements. Results indicate that this material exhibits s-wave superconductivity, characterized by a transition temperature (Tc) of approximately 3.5 K. Furthermore, the specific heat data suggest a two-band superconducting model.

This study examines the application of NLP methods to retrieve bug reports that are textually identical to a specific query. The research evaluates a diverse set of techniques, including both traditional and deep learning-based models, to assess their effectiveness. The findings demonstrate that these NLP approaches significantly enhance the retrieval of exact matches compared to standard baseline models. Additionally, the authors investigate the potential of these methods to identify bug reports that convey semantic similarity to the query.

We present a highly effective field theory for the Fermi surface of graphene, which captures the influence of the Fermi surface's geometry on the system's phase transitions. This model includes a mechanism for a superconducting instability and a novel instability leading to a spin-density wave (SDW) phase. We demonstrate that the strong coupling regime of this theory exhibits a first-order transition to an SDW phase, a phenomenon not observed in conventional Fermi liquids.

This study introduces a self-training framework designed to enhance Named Entity Recognition (NER) models. The framework utilizes a teacher-student architecture where both initial teachers and students are trained on the same dataset, subsequently employing the teacher's predictions to augment the training data for the student. Experiments conducted on the OntoNotes 5.0 dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms the baseline model, achieving F1-scores of 85.10% for the student model and 85.12% for the teacher model.

The tourism sector is a global powerhouse, generating billions in revenue and serving as a primary livelihood for millions worldwide. In recent years, the travel and hospitality landscape has been transformed by the proliferation of social media, which offers travelers diverse options and feedback from fellow users. This study examines tourism-related data from Twitter to uncover patterns and insights that can inform industry strategies. We employ a specialized approach to extract location-specific data from the platform, which is then analyzed to understand the nature of these conversations. The results of this analysis are visualized through interactive maps, providing a user-friendly tool for applying these discoveries to practical business applications.

We report the detection of a companion to the young star CI Tau at a projected separation of 0.12 arcseconds, corresponding to 17 au. Utilizing the Keck/NIRC2 adaptive optics system, we employed Angular Differential Imaging (ADI) to identify the companion, which exhibits a contrast of 4.5 magnitudes in the K-band. Radial velocity measurements indicate the companion is moving at 1.2 km/s relative to CI Tau. This result effectively rules out planet migration driven by the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect, as the observed motion is significantly lower than the minimum required to explain the system's current architecture.

This study examines the correspondence between free movement on a sphere under an $l=0$ centrifugal barrier potential and finite-energy trajectories of a particle moving freely in three-dimensional Euclidean space. It is demonstrated that zero-energy states within this spherical potential map precisely onto the closure of a line in free-space paths. Furthermore, finite-duration scattering processes at the spherical potential level correspond to infinite-duration paths in Euclidean space.

This study investigates the existence of non-trivial solutions for non-local integro-differential equations subject to specific boundary conditions, where these operators may exhibit singularities. Our approach hinges on demonstrating that the associated problem defined by the operator and boundary conditions admits only the trivial solution.

This paper introduces a solution for multi-object filtering in unlabelled frameworks, which avoids the combinatorial explosion inherent in labelled approaches. It further enhances trajectory estimation capabilities by integrating data association with the proposed solution, which outperforms the standard particle filter method in terms of both speed and accuracy, particularly when dealing with occlusions and clutter.

This paper proposes a novel stability assessment criterion for large-scale power systems with significant converter penetration, utilizing the energy-based method. Unlike traditional approaches that depend on small-signal stability analysis, this proposed criterion evaluates system stability by examining the trajectories of state variables. The study applies this criterion to a 39-bus system with high wind penetration, demonstrating its validity through various fault scenarios. Furthermore, the paper investigates the influence of control parameters on the criterion's assessment outcomes.

This study introduces a novel approach to constructing signature templates designed to enhance the accuracy of forensic tools for detecting forged documents. The proposed method integrates three key characteristics: distinctiveness, complexity, and repeatability. By applying a new metric to evaluate and measure these attributes, the system identifies and extracts the most significant features from raw data. Experimental results demonstrate that this strategy significantly boosts the effectiveness of forgery detection, achieving a 10% improvement in performance when tested against 1000 signatures. Additionally, the system's robustness is validated by its ability to maintain performance levels even when operating with a limited dataset of only 10 signatures.

This work explores Hardy sums as weighted directed geodesics on the modular group. We establish a Hardy sum weight function satisfying specific requirements, which allows us to derive two distinct Dirichlet series representations for Hardy sums. Furthermore, we establish various multiplicative identities and divergent series formulas for these sums.

The widespread adoption of smartphones has made mobile applications a cornerstone of daily life. As the number of apps grows, so does the complexity of their use, prompting the need for more intuitive and personalized user experiences. Customization is a key strategy to meet these needs, yet it is often hindered by the high effort required to configure it manually. To address this, we introduce a new method for automatically tailoring mobile applications by leveraging persistent context. This approach captures contextual data from a user's past interactions within an app and utilizes it to automate configuration settings. Our evaluation, based on a user study involving 20 participants, demonstrates that this approach successfully generates novel interface configurations that are both understandable and beneficial to users.

This study introduces a new framework for pose estimation that delivers real-time results by integrating a coarse-to-fine strategy with a multi-scale feature pyramid. The system employs a dual-stream architecture to process both color and depth data, enabling the prediction of 6 degrees of freedom (DoF) for 3D keypoints. The depth-based stream leverages a pyramid of multi-scale features to generate precise 3D keypoint estimates, while the color-based stream focuses on predicting 3D relative pose. These outputs are then combined to derive the final global pose. The model's effectiveness was validated on the real-world real-world RGB-D dataset, where it achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.018 meters and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.024 meters.

This study details the performance of AstroSat's Cadmium-Zinc-Telluride (CZT) imaging spectrometer, which operates within the 17–225 keV range. The instrument's collimator, featuring a 10° field of view and 1° angular resolution, was evaluated using data from the AstroSat mission. The collimator's performance was validated through observations of the Crab pulsar and Cygnus X-1, which were measured within the detector's field of view. The resulting flux measurements for these sources align with established literature values, confirming the reliability of the flux determination. Additionally, the instrument's capabilities were assessed by analyzing the spectra of the Crab pulsar and Cygnus X-1, as well as the light curves of the Crab pulsar and the Sco X-1 source. The study further reports the first-ever detection of the 222 keV line from the Crab pulsar, which was identified in the AstroSat data.

Blockchain protocols are broadly categorized into those that are permissionless and those that are permissioned. This paper focuses on the former class, specifically examining the impact of node-level application layer failures on the protocol's resilience. We introduce a new methodology for analyzing this impact, utilizing a framework of continuous time Markov chains to model the operational dynamics of individual nodes. Furthermore, we investigate the phenomenon of stragglers—nodes that experience delays in message transmission and processing—and analyze their detrimental effects on overall network performance.

This study examines the impact of the standard model's instability scale on Higgs mass constraints within extended models, specifically focusing on the two-Higgs doublet model (2HDM) and the minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM). We demonstrate that accounting for the standard model's instability scale significantly relaxes lower limits on the Higgs mass in both frameworks. Specifically, in the 2HDM, incorporating this effect allows the Higgs mass to be as low as approximately 120 GeV, whereas in the MSSM, it permits values near 110 GeV.

This study demonstrates that the Hamilton-Jacobi equation associated with the $p$-Talagrand inequality within Carnot groups corresponds to the $p$-gradient flow of the $p$-Talagrand entropy on the probability simplex.

This paper introduces an Exponentially Weighted Divergence (EWD) estimator for univariate and multivariate nonparametric density estimation. The estimator is derived from a novel class of divergence measures, the Exponentially Weighted Divergences (EWDs), which are constructed by integrating Density Power Divergences (DPDs) with exponential functions. The primary advantage of using EWDs is that they allow for the control of bias and robustness through a single parameter. This study introduces a new method for segmenting the background from foreground content in image sequences. The proposed algorithm first classifies pixels into static or motion-centric categories, followed by the application of a Markov Random Field (MRF) model to distinguish foreground pixels. Experimental results indicate that the algorithm achieves high performance across various datasets, including those with significant background movement, complex foregrounds, and those containing both moving foreground and moving background elements.

We investigate the statistical characteristics of the characteristic polynomials of $2 \times 2$ integer matrices with determinant $-1$ and entries restricted to $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. These polynomials correspond to the periodic orbits of the shift map defined on the space of bi-infinite sequences over the ternary alphabet $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. Our findings indicate that the variability of the polynomial's coefficients is notably elevated when the associated periodic orbits contain self-intersections. We demonstrate that the density of such self-intersections is governed by the count of distinct periodic orbits of equivalent length, and we establish a universal upper bound for this density applicable to all shift maps.

We introduce a new classification system for periodic variable stars, which categorizes them into three distinct groups: (1) eclipsing binaries, (2) nebular variables (NEB), and (3) other periodic variables. This system leverages the unique periodicity of eclipsing binaries and NEB variables, which exhibit periodic changes in their spectral line profiles. By applying the Fourier transform to time-series spectral data, we identify periodicity in these line profiles, enabling the differentiation of eclipsing binaries from NEB variables. Additionally, we have developed a pipeline to automatically classify these two types and extract their periods. The pipeline was tested on a sample of 1,000 OGLE-II variables, successfully identifying 1,000 eclipsing binaries and 1,000 NEB variables. The results demonstrate that the pipeline is capable of accurately classifying these two types and determining their periods.

This paper addresses the issue of deriving a non-negative imaginary system from a LTI system characterized by a non-negative imaginary system response. The study establishes a specific geometric framework for identifying the nearest negative imaginary system within a prescribed low-dimensional subspace defined by the coefficients of a rational representation.

This study investigates End-to-Eend Automatic Speech Recognition (E2E-ASR) within continual learning frameworks. We introduce a continual learning algorithm that utilizes a single model to handle a sequence of tasks without any retraining for new challenges. This approach is evaluated on the E2E-ASR task using the LibriSpeech corpus, where distinct tasks are defined by different hours of audio data from various speakers. Our findings indicate that our method achieves a substantial reduction in error rates for new tasks—improving by 20% to 40% compared to conventional fine-tuning. Furthermore, our method outperforms current state-of-the-art continual learning techniques by 10% to 30% in terms of error reduction for new tasks.

Sentiment analysis is a vital component of social media analytics, yet it faces significant hurdles when applied to code-switching contexts, where users mix languages within a single message. This study introduces a novel approach for analyzing sentiment in messages that blend English and Arabic. The proposed method employs a two-stage architecture: the initial phase involves a two-layer Conditional Random Field (CRF) model designed to identify specific code-switching segments, followed by a second phase that utilizes a two-layer Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to forecast sentiment. The entire system is trained using a combined dataset of English and Arabic. The model's performance is evaluated on a benchmark dataset containing 10,000 instances from the Arabic Sentiment140 corpus. The results demonstrate that this approach achieves a 75.4% F1-score, outperforming existing baseline methods.

This study examines the three-loop seesaw model, which extends the minimal framework by incorporating three heavy neutrinos. We demonstrate that this approach can yield a neutrino mass scale consistent with experimental data, all while maintaining the parameters within the existing two-loop model's constraints. Specifically, we show that a sterile particle with a mass under 129 GeV can be accommodated, enabling detectable signatures at the Large Hadron Collider. Furthermore, we analyze the lepton flavor violation predictions, forecasting a significant signal for the muon-to-electron conversion ratio ($\mu \to e$) in upcoming experiments.

This study introduces a novel architecture for Product-based Neural Networks (PNNs) designed to handle tabular data. The proposed PNN structure is engineered to capture correlations between categorical variables by leveraging the relationships inherent in product features. To address the challenge of determining optimal network topologies, we introduce a new pruning strategy that selects the most effective PNN structure based on a specific criterion. Experiments on various real-world datasets demonstrate that this approach yields superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

This study investigates active reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted active transmitting beamforming design in millimeter-wave (mmWave) networks. The primary objective is to maximize the minimum achievable rate for all users by jointly optimizing transmit beamforming at the base station (BS) and passive reflection coefficients at the IRS. The challenge is complicated by channel state information (CSI) uncertainty affecting both the uplink and downlink, as well as the practical limitations of IRS hardware, which restricts reflection coefficients to a unit modulus. To address these constraints, we introduce a novel algorithm based on the sequential convex optimization (SCO) framework. This approach ensures a unit modulus for IRS coefficients by employing a two-step design: first, it optimizes the transmit beamforming and an auxiliary variable; second, it optimizes the IRS phase shifts using a projection step. The resulting algorithm is proven to be computationally efficient and converges to a stationary point. Furthermore, we derive an upper bound on the suboptimality of the proposed solution. Numerical simulations confirm the algorithm's low computational complexity, rapid convergence, and superior performance compared to existing methods.

Branch prediction is a pivotal component of modern CPUs, and dynamic prediction methods are increasingly employed to enhance performance. This study introduces a dynamic predictor that leverages deep learning algorithms, contrasting it with a baseline using a standard table lookup predictor. The experiments reveal that dynamic prediction significantly outperforms the static approach. Furthermore, the investigation examines various deep learning models, evaluating their accuracy and efficiency, and the results indicate that a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network achieves superior branch prediction accuracy.

This paper introduces a deep convolutional neural network designed to autonomously manage a PTZ camera for monitoring a predefined target. The system operates by analyzing a video feed from the PTZ unit to generate control commands that adjust the camera's pan, tilt, and zoom functions. The proposed architecture comprises a deep neural network with 12 layers, which incorporates a specialized component to identify and correct image distortion. Experimental results demonstrate that this method outperforms conventional techniques in both maintaining the target within the visual frame and sustaining accurate tracking.

This study demonstrates that the two-dimensional SOS model possesses non-trivial non-normalisable boundary conditions, where such laws do not depend on the bulk's state. Consequently, these findings establish the existence of scale-invariant (critical) layers at an interface, indicating that the system exhibits critical behavior.

This study introduces a new method for characterizing the effective rate coefficient ($K_{E2P}$) for entangled two-photon resonance energy transfer (E2P). The approach utilizes the decay of a donor's population, monitored via time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy following excitation by a two-photon pulse. This technique is applied to investigate the E2P occurring between the $S_1$ states of biphenyl molecules within a bipphenyl-dibenzanthrone (DBA) system. The findings demonstrate that $K_{E2P}$ is highly sensitive to the concentration of DBA, reaching a maximum value of $1.0 \times 10^{-10} \text{ cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$ at a DBA concentration of $1.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ M}$.

This study examines the mass spectrum of bottom baryons using light-cone QCD sum rules. We calculate strong coupling constants for various decay modes involving bottom baryons and mesons, which subsequently allow for the determination of masses for the newly predicted bottom baryons. The resulting strong coupling constants align well with those derived from large $N_c$ QCD and potential models. Furthermore, the predicted bottom baryon masses are consistent with results obtained through Q sum rules, the light-cone sum rule method, and the Bethe-Salpeter equation. Finally, the study offers predictions for strong coupling constants in the decays of bottom baryons into excited bottom baryons and pions, which may assist future experimental searches for these states.

This study examines how new physics models can accommodate anomalies found in recent short-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments. We investigate the compatibility of these anomalies with both the Muon $g-2$ anomaly and the $(g-2)_\mu$ measurement from the LHCb experiment. Our analysis reveals that a viable solution exists using an extended $L_\mu-L_\tau$ model featuring two heavy right-handed neutrinos and two new gauge bosons, $Z_\mu$ and $Z_\tau$. We further explore the phenomenology of this framework, specifically focusing on the lepton flavor-violating decay $\mu \to e\gamma$ and the decay of $\mu \to \tau$ neutrinos.

This paper demonstrates that the "implied weights" generated by linear regression techniques, such as propensity score weighting, can be utilized to design optimal observational studies for causal inference. We establish that minimizing the mean squared error of these weights constitutes an optimal strategy for designing such studies. Additionally, we introduce a straightforward method for estimating these weights using a propensity score model and prove that these estimates are asymptotically normal. Finally, we illustrate the practical application of our proposed framework through a case study involving the analysis of COVID-19 data.

The increasing integration of power converters into modern grids has highlighted the critical need for voltage source converters (VSCs) to detect, identify, and mitigate oscillations. This study introduces a new control strategy for VSCs that enables the detection and damping of both inter-area and local oscillations. The approach utilizes VSCs installed at specific nodes to enhance damping, thereby reducing the necessity for extensive placement of power system stabilizers (PSS) on generators. Furthermore, the proposed method addresses oscillations by adjusting the active and reactive power outputs of the VSCs. Theoretical analysis confirms the efficacy of this control scheme, which is also validated through simulations using a modified IEEE 118-bus system.

We introduce a theoretical framework for analyzing the quantum behavior of light emitted by a thermally excited collection of atoms undergoing collective decay. This approach utilizes a generalized master equation for the light field, derived from the microscopic dynamics of the atomic ensemble. The model is validated by demonstrating that the emitted light exhibits sub-Poissonian statistics, specifically showing anti-bunching in the two-atom limit. Furthermore, we examine the quantum properties of the emitted light as a function of atomic density, revealing a transition from collective to independent emission when the interatomic spacing exceeds a specific threshold.

This study examines the stability of kinks in nonlinear field theories featuring internal modes. Utilizing the background field method, we derive a perturbative framework to analyze the corrections to the kink's mass and interaction with the mode it couples with. The analysis demonstrates that perturbation theory accurately predicts the kink's stability when examined at a suitable scale. Furthermore, the work offers a clear interpretation of the zero mode within perturbation theory.

Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) are essential for characterizing exclusive hadron production, high-energy scattering, and the internal three-dimensional structure of nucleons. This study examines the evolution of GPDs within the context of the non-linear DGLAP framework, utilizing a leading-order (LO) calculation for the one-loop splitting function. We demonstrate that the splitting function can be expressed as a function of the nucleon's momentum fraction $x$ and an additional variable, $z$, which represents the nucleon's longitudinal coherence length. This formulation facilitates a direct connection between GPDs and parton distribution functions (PDFs). Furthermore, we derive analytical expressions for the splitting function at both the LO and next-to-leading order (NLO) levels. Finally, we present the LO splitting function for the pion, kaon, and proton, and provide a comparison with results from NLO proton splitting functions derived via the order-momentum scheme.

Text classification is a prevalent natural language processing task, yet it is highly susceptible to discrete noise, which can drastically alter the model's decision boundary. This study introduces a straightforward yet effective method for identifying and correcting discrete noise within the training dataset. By applying the $L_2$ norm to measure the similarity between documents, we evaluate the efficacy of our proposed solution across multiple benchmarks. The results demonstrate that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques, achieving an F1 score of 0.949 on the AG News dataset and a score of 0.919 on the 20Newsgroups dataset.

Accurate polyp detection is essential for performing endoscopic surgery. Although deep learning has achieved significant success in this domain, existing methods often struggle to aggregate features effectively, particularly in areas where the polyp is indistinct. To address this, we introduce a novel channel-aware attention mechanism designed to enhance feature aggregation. This module leverages the distinct correlation between channels to weight features, thereby highlighting polyp-relevant information. Furthermore, we propose a new loss function that integrates the Dice coefficient and a modified version of the IoU loss to optimize the balance between recall and precision. Extensive experiments on the Kvasir-SEG and ETIS-Seg datasets confirm that our approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods. The source code is publicly accessible at https://github.com/chenx1996/Polyp-ACC-Aggregation.

This paper introduces a sequential sampling technique to draw samples of size $n$ from a finite population, where the degree of dispersal is governed by a user-defined constant, $c$. The expected number of draws equals $n$ when the setting $c=1$; however, adjusting $c$ to values greater than or equal to 1 allows for a controlled increase in spread.

The rp-process, occurring during Type-I X-ray bursts, involves the rapid proton capture of nuclei at temperatures exceeding $10^9$ K. This study examines the process's dynamics within the CNO region, utilizing the MESA stellar evolution code to model the composition of the X-ray burst flame. We specifically investigate the impact of nuclear reaction rates on the ${}^{56}$Ni nuclear statistical equilibrium (NSE) valley, which acts as a waiting point in the rp-process. Our findings indicate that approximately 20% of the NSE material flows past the ${}^{56}$Ni waiting point. This conclusion is reached by analyzing the NSE evolution of the flame, which is governed by the competition between nuclear reaction rates and the expansion timescale.

This paper extends Drinfeld's description regarding the irreducible components of the special fiber of $Sh(4,4)$ to an arbitrary characteristic $p>0$. The study establishes that the flat parts of these components correspond precisely to torsion cosets within $p$-divisible groups of the abelian scheme, and further proves the result that any such part contains exactly $p$ irreducible components.

Recent Very High Energy (VHE) gamma-ray observations have significantly advanced our understanding of the galactic gamma-ray emission mechanisms. This review outlines the current state of research regarding the VHE origin of these emissions, covering both resolved and unresolved components. The discussion includes the impact of the latest VHE data on the cosmic-ray origin problem, alongside the proposed connection between cosmic-ray acceleration and the non-thermal emissions observed in supernova remnants.

This study examines the large-time behavior of diffusion systems governed by nonlocal boundary conditions, where the interaction kernel is independent of the domain's geometry. We demonstrate that the asymptotic dynamics are characterized by the first eigenfunction of a specific integral operator, and we establish a new theorem regarding the unique existence and stability of eigenpairs for this operator.

We applied a machine learning approach to categorize compact stellar systems (CSSs) into elliptical and spheroidal types. Utilizing a dataset of 1,000 objects drawn from the NASA Extragalactic Database, we employed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to identify the most effective color indices for classification. Our results indicate that blue and red colors hold the highest information value, followed by green and yellow. Additionally, the CNN demonstrated superior performance compared to a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. These findings suggest that the CNN is capable of detecting subtle structural variations within CSSs.

This paper presents a simulation framework designed to assist in the construction of Recommender Systems (RS). It enables the evaluation of various RS designs by comparing their performance across different data distributions, thereby supporting informed decision-making. The simulation environment is built on the ReccSim toolkit, which offers a comprehensive suite of tools for RS development and assessment. It supports data generation and manipulation, the construction of data-driven simulations, and the orchestration of experiments. The paper details the simulation's architecture, illustrates its application through a concrete example, and outlines its primary functions.

This study introduces a hypothesis testing method applicable to distributions characterized by infinite mean or variance, such as those with heavy tails. The approach utilizes truncated sample means to estimate the distribution function, offering robustness against outliers and heavy tails. We demonstrate that the test statistic derived from these truncated samples converges in distribution to a Brownian bridge. Furthermore, we establish that the test achieves asymptotic power against contiguous alternatives. The effectiveness of this method is validated through simulations and real-world data analysis.

Deep learning has become a cornerstone in developing Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs), with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) being the most prevalent architecture. However, CNNs suffer from significant drawbacks, including a high demand for extensive training data and a lack of interpretability. Furthermore, these models often fail to fully leverage the inherent sparsity and temporal characteristics of EEG signals. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel BCI framework that integrates a Wavelet Neural Network (WNN) with a CNN. This approach utilizes a Wavelet Transform to extract features from EEG data, capitalizing on the method's ability to handle sparsity and non-stationarity. The extracted features are then processed by the CNN to derive the final classification. The proposed model was evaluated on a public dataset for a two-class motor imagery task. Results indicate that this method surpasses existing state-of-the-art approaches, achieving an accuracy of 98.1%.

This study examines the dynamics of a massive scalar field within the noncommutative $AdS$ framework, utilizing the $AdS/CFT$ correspondence to derive the corresponding noncommutative non-scalars field theory. We calculate the two-point correlation function for the field and apply the $Leutwyler$ method to derive the solvable spectral density, subsequently generating the two-point function of the scalar operator via the $AdS/CFT$ relation. Furthermore, we investigate the thermal behavior of the field and the scalar operator function, demonstrating that noncommutativity influences the thermal spectrum.

This study examines kidney transplantation allocation policies within a stochastic framework, specifically focusing on the acceptance/rejection dichotomy and the impact of graft incompatibility. We model the system using a Markov Decision Process (MDS) that includes additional state variables to capture incompatibility. Our findings demonstrate that neglecting these factors leads to an underestimation of the social welfare value associated with accepting a transplant. Furthermore, we show that failing to account for acceptance decisions can result in inefficient policies, such as those that never utilize a donor's organs.

This study investigates the geometric characteristics of latent representations produced by both Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. We demonstrate that HMM latent spaces adhere to a manifold structure, where each latent state corresponds to a specific hidden state. In contrast, LSTM latent spaces are approximately linearly separable, with each latent state approximating a linear subspace defined by recurrent state inputs. These findings are supported by theoretical analysis and empirical validation. Furthermore, we establish a link between these latent spaces and the concept of "soft" hidden states in HMMs. Leveraging this connection, we introduce a method to convert HMMs into LSTMs capable of replicating the original HMM's state sequences.

This work investigates the compactness and membership within the Schatten classes of weighted Bergman space $L^p$ for operators $T_f$ defined by multiplication. We establish conditions under which such operators are compact and belong to the Schatten class $B_p^S$ for $0 < p < \infty$. Additionally, we analyze the $p$-order Schatten norm for these operators, deriving a formula for its calculation. Finally, we demonstrate that the mapping $T_f \mapsto T_g$ constitutes a bounded linear operator from the multiplier space $B_p^S$ to itself, a result that holds significant implications for the study of weighted Bergman space algebras.

This study evaluates various compression techniques for pre-trained language models (PLMs) across text classification and question answering tasks. We assessed the impact of different strategies on model performance and efficiency, including layer and attention head pruning, as well as the recently introduced knowledge distillation approach known as "distillation without a teacher" (DIT). Our findings indicate that for text classification, the H2O architecture delivers an optimal balance between compression and accuracy. Conversely, in question answering tasks, layer pruning emerges as the superior method. Additionally, the performance of attention head pruning is highly sensitive to the specific dataset employed.

The article proposes that "metascience"—a new endeavor focused on the collective development of data analysis tools and methodologies—emerge as a vital field within high energy physics (HEP). This initiative aims to address the challenges posed by the exponential growth of data volumes and the increasing complexity of scientific endeavors. The author argues that metascience is essential for sustaining high-quality research output and accelerating the pace of discovery. The proposal is supported by several key points: (1) the necessity of a unified metaprogram to advance novel methods and tools for the collective benefit of the community; (2) the imperative to adopt metaprograms as a standard practice, particularly to ensure the reproducibility of results; (3) the significant contributions metaprograms make to the broader scientific community; and (4) the need to implement rigorous quality assurance protocols for the methods and tools developed within these frameworks.

We present an inductive construction for generalized Howe curves and their corresponding decomposed Richelot isogenies, which extends the approach originally introduced by Howe. This method is particularly effective for generating curves with significant Richelot isogeny cycles. Furthermore, we establish a direct relationship between decomposed Richelot isogenies and commuting Richelot transformations, which are special forms of Weil descent isogenies. Finally, we illustrate the application of our decomposition framework to three distinct scenarios: cycles of length 2, length 16, and length 32.

We report the discovery of three magnetic hot subdwarfs (mHDs) with spectral types ranging from sdO10 to sdOB10, identified through the analysis of 10,000 spectra from the HST/STIS archive. These newly found objects, designated as SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111, SDSS1013+0111

This paper introduces a methodology for analyzing approximation errors for errors in matrices by leveraging invariant matrix theory. The approach involves applying the matrix exponential to an error matrix, enabling a structured analysis of error evolution over time. We utilize invariant subspaces to decompose the error evolution into distinct components, which facilitates the identification of dominant error sources. The analysis is demonstrated through a case study involving matrix approximation errors in the context of the Koopman operator.

This study examines the distribution of short URLs within Wikipedia articles, analyzing both raw wikitext and transformed HTML to determine the visibility of hyperlink-specific attributes. Our findings indicate that HTML contains substantially fewer short URLs than wikitext, with HTML often omitting links to external websites or replacing them with placeholder text. Additionally, we observe that the textual content associated with these external links in HTML is typically more concise compared to the links embedded in the raw wikitext.

The interplay between twisted bilayers and ferroelectrics offers a pathway to create novel topological and electronic states. In this study, we examine the polar domains within twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) and their potential for engineering new physics. Our findings indicate that the polarization of individual polar domains can be controlled through the application of a gate voltage. We further demonstrate that the domain walls separating these regions can be tuned to host flat electronic bands, making them a promising platform for investigating topological phenomena. Additionally, the presence of these polar domains can facilitate the formation of a ferroelectric superlattice, which may enable the creation of a p-n junction. Finally, we explore the potential for creating a Josephson junction by connecting two distinct polar domains via a narrow TBG channel.

This study examines how light travels in a spherically symmetric universe with a non-flat geometry. We derive the null geodesics and the deflection angle for a light ray, while also analyzing the properties of the effective potential. By employing perturbation theory, we derived an analytical approximation for the deflection angle valid within the weak deflection regime. Our findings indicate that in a non-flat universe, light propagation differs significantly from that in a flat universe, a distinction reflected in the unique characteristics of the effective potential and the light ray's deflection angle.

We investigate the dynamics of a single colloid suspended in a liquid crystal within a channel featuring a wave-like surface composed of alternating hills and valleys. Our findings indicate that this specific wall configuration significantly influences colloid trajectories, with the effect intensifying as the surface undulates more sharply. We attribute this phenomenon to the formation of a $\pi$-phase shift in the liquid crystal's orientation at the troughs, which generates localized flow circulations.

The Roche limit defines the minimum distance at which tidal forces can disrupt a celestial body. For an asteroid, the limit is inversely proportional to its elongation; thus, more elongated bodies become susceptible to tidal disruption at distances significantly greater than the Roche limit. This study investigates the tidal disruption of a rapidly rotating, elongated, rubble-pile asteroid, modeled as a triaxial ellipsoid with a density of 2,000 kg/m³. We present a new analytical formula for the tidal disruption distance, which is applicable to any triaxial ellipsoid. Our results indicate that for a triaxial asteroid with a density of 2,000 kg/m³ and an axis ratio of 1.5, tidal disruption can occur at approximately 1.5 times the standard Roche limit.

Machine learning (ML) and quantum computing (QC) are increasingly converging to address challenges in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. This paper demonstrates that combining ML and QC can significantly enhance the study of rare conformational transitions. We present a case study involving the folding of a 21-residue protein, where we developed a supervised ML model to predict the energy of specific protein conformations. This model was trained on a dataset generated by simulating quantum annealing on the D-Wave quantum processor. The ML model successfully identified the global energy minimum and predicted energies for other local minima with high accuracy. Furthermore, we utilized the ML model to construct a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) trajectory, employing a technique called quantum-enhanced sampling to efficiently explore the energy landscape. The results indicate that this hybrid approach is effective for investigating rare conformational transitions in biomolecules.

We introduce MAPPIES, a novel Monte-Carlo code designed to simulate the polarisation of X-ray and gamma-ray photons emitted from celestial bodies. The software accurately models photon interactions with matter, including Compton scattering, photoelectric absorption, and pair production, while also accounting for polarisation effects arising from these processes. Additionally, it incorporates photon energy degradation due to repeated Compton scattering events. The code's validity is confirmed through comparisons with analytical solutions for Compton scattering and existing Monte-Carlo simulations. Its utility is demonstrated by applying it to a magnetar model to simulate polarised emission spectra.

This study examines the seasonal development of categories in sea-ice thickness within a 2D numerical model, incorporating a parameterized wind-driven melt ponding process. The model is subjected to varying boundary conditions, including open water and closed sea scenarios, as well as varying levels of wind-driven melt ponding. The analysis reveals that melt ponding significantly alters the seasonal evolution of sea-ice thickness categories. Specifically, when open water is present, melt ponding intensifies the seasonal cycle of ice thickness. The model demonstrates that melt ponding can be effectively represented as a parameterized process, with the impact of melt ponding on the seasonal evolution of sea-ice thickness categories being strongly dependent on the initial conditions of sea-ice thickness.

We present the families of curves $\mathcal{X}_{a,b,n,s}$ and $\mathcal{Y}_{n,s}$ over $\mathbb{C}$, which serve as specific types of cyclic $n$-coverings of Hermitian curves defined by distinct parameters. For these families, we determine the genus, the number of singular points, and the singular tangent directions. Additionally, we compute the multiplicity of the Weierstrass points within the normalization of each curve and define the quotient curves obtained by dividing by the respective cyclic $n$-action.

Singing voice synthesis has evolved rapidly over the past decade, driven by significant strides in deep learning. However, despite these advancements, the field has not yet reached a point of commercial maturity. This study presents a systematic review of singing voice synthesis research, covering both academic developments and commercial progress. We begin by outlining the core challenges and core tasks of the technology. Next, we examine the most critical technical hurdles and the prevailing solutions used to address them. We also explore the primary evaluation metrics used to assess performance. Finally, we analyze the future trajectory of singing voice synthesis, considering both ongoing academic inquiries and recent commercial developments.

This study introduces NIPS4Bplus, an advanced version of the NIPS4B bird song dataset, featuring recordings from 14 distinct species captured across three distinct environments: a forest, a meadow, and a coastal area. The collection was conducted using autonomous recorders, and the audio data underwent precise species-level annotation. The NIPS4Bplus dataset comprises a total of 1,500 recordings, each lasting 30 seconds. The provided materials include the raw audio files, the labeled dataset, and the corresponding annotation software. The authors demonstrate that NIPSip4Bplus serves as a valuable resource for advancing ecoacoustic research and bird population monitoring. The code utilized for annotation is available on GitHub, and the dataset can be downloaded from the iNaturalist website.

We introduce a unified, model-based framework for jointly performing intrinsic and extrinsic calibration of event-based cameras using frame-based cameras. This method estimates a set of extrinsic parameters that define the rigid transformation from event camera coordinates to frame-based coordinates. By leveraging the correspondence between point features in one frame and event streams in the other, our framework generates a set of geometric constraints. These constraints are derived from the projection of 3D world points into both sensors and subsequently refined through the application of frame-based camera calibration. The proposed approach is robust to noise, resilient to outliers, and capable of estimating precise extrinsic calibration parameters. We demonstrate the efficacy of this framework through a comprehensive experimental evaluation.

Graph learning has proven effective across diverse domains, including social networks, e-commerce, knowledge graphs, and biological and medical data. Despite this success, the field has not yet established a unified framework for graph representation learning. This paper reviews recent advances in graph representation learning, aiming to provide a comprehensive overview of the field. We introduce a taxonomy that classifies these methods based on the specific information utilized during the learning process. Additionally, we examine various graph learning tasks and their corresponding algorithms, while also addressing potential future research directions.

This study introduces a 3D guidance system for retinal surgery that utilizes a projector to create a visual representation of a plane on the patient's retina. By projecting a circular light spot, the system indicates the surgical plane; when the spot appears as a single point, the cutting plane is aligned perfectly with the target. Deviations from the ideal position manifest as elliptical projections, where the orientation and elongation of the visual shape indicate the specific direction and magnitude of the required adjustment. The system's effectiveness was validated through experiments conducted on a human eye model, demonstrating its ability to provide accurate three-dimensional guidance during the procedure.

We establish that the $F$-polynomials associated with cluster algebras of type $A$ adhere to a product formula. This product can be decomposed into a summation over the roots of the corresponding cluster monomials.

The FIDO2 standard, developed by the FIDO Alliance, is driving the adoption of passwordless authentication. This paper investigates how FIDO2 can be adapted for use in the Internet of Things (IoT) domain. We introduce a framework that enables resource-constrained IoT devices to utilize FIDO2, allowing them to issue cryptographic proofs of identity and authenticate themselves to a central server. Our approach is designed to be flexible enough to accommodate various device capabilities and to integrate with different key management strategies. We demonstrate the practicality of this framework by implementing it on a low-power microcontroller and confirming its effectiveness through a practical demonstration.
